title: This is my body, this is my blood of the new testament — the Passover kept and filled, the covenant cut with both houses (Exodus 12 and 24; Jeremiah 31; Isaiah 25)
summary:
It ain't new. The night he was betrayed he kept the Passover as Moses gave it, bread and cup at the table, and said what the bread and the cup were:

*And as they were eating, Yahusha (Jesus) took bread, and blessed it, and brake it, and gave it to the disciples, and said, Take, eat; this is my body.* (Matthew 26:26)

*For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.* (Matthew 26:28)

The meal was the feast Moses set for ever, not a new rite put in its place:

*And this day shall be unto you for a memorial; and ye shall keep it a feast to Yahuah (LORD) throughout your generations; ye shall keep it a feast by an ordinance for ever.* (Exodus 12:14)

Paul says the lamb of that feast is who was sacrificed, and the feast is still kept:

*Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Messiah (Christ) our passover is sacrificed for us:* (1 Corinthians 5:7)

*Therefore let us keep the feast, not with old leaven, neither with the leaven of malice and wickedness; but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.* (1 Corinthians 5:8)

*My blood of the new testament*: a covenant is cut in blood, and the first one was. Moses sprinkled the people and said the same words over the same thing:

*And Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said, Behold the blood of the covenant, which Yahuah (LORD) hath made with you concerning all these words.* (Exodus 24:8)

The new covenant is Jeremiah's, and Jeremiah names the parties. Not a church in place of a people, but the two houses of the one people, with the Torah written where it was always meant to live:

*Behold, the days come, saith Yahuah (LORD), that I will make a new covenant with the house of Yashar'el (Israel), and with the house of Yahudah (Judah):* (Jeremiah 31:31)

*But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Yashar'el (Israel); After those days, saith Yahuah (LORD), I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their Elohim (God), and they shall be my people.* (Jeremiah 31:33)

The blood does what the Torah said blood does:

*For the life of the flesh is in the blood: and I have given it to you upon the altar to make an atonement for your souls: for it is the blood that maketh an atonement for the soul.* (Leviticus 17:11)

And the one whose blood it is was named at the river before any of it:

*The next day John seeth Yahusha (Jesus) coming unto him, and saith, Behold the Lamb of Elohim (God), which taketh away the sin of the world.* (John 1:29)

He stops drinking the cup until a day he names:

*But I say unto you, I will not drink henceforth of this fruit of the vine, until that day when I drink it new with you in my Father’s kingdom.* (Matthew 26:29)

That day is the feast on the mountain the prophet spread, and John saw the same supper from the other end:

*And in this mountain shall Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) make unto all people a feast of fat things, a feast of wines on the lees, of fat things full of marrow, of wines on the lees well refined.* (Isaiah 25:6)

*And he saith unto me, Write, Blessed are they which are called unto the marriage supper of the Lamb. And he saith unto me, These are the true sayings of Elohim (God).* (Revelation 19:9)

A Passover kept, a covenant cut in blood as the first was, made with both houses, Torah on the heart, and a cup set down until the feast in the kingdom. Nothing at the table was done away; everything at the table was filled.

3030.prose: Mark sets the same meal beside Matthew's. Same bread, same hands, same words at the table. At the Passover Yahusha (Jesus) said *this is my body* over the bread, and two men tell it alike, with nothing in either telling that puts the feast aside.
3030.phrase: took bread, and blessed, and brake it, and gave to them
3030.sentence: Mark gives the same bread, blessing, breaking and giving, so the Passover table is witnessed twice.

3031.prose: Luke tells who sat at the table: the twelve, when the hour came. What Matthew shows being done with the bread was done in front of them, at the meal Luke names in the next lines as the Passover.
3031.phrase: when the hour was come, he sat down
3031.sentence: Luke shows him seated with the twelve when the hour came, the company the bread was given to.

3032.prose: Paul received it and passed it on. It is the supper of the night Yahusha (Jesus) was betrayed, the same bread Matthew sets at the Passover table. Paul says he was handed it and gave it on, so the bread is no later invention.
3032.phrase: the same night in which he was betrayed took bread
3032.sentence: Paul says he received and delivered the supper of the night of the betrayal, the same bread Matthew records.

3033.prose: This is where the Passover starts. Yahuah (LORD) speaks to Moses and Aaron in Egypt and gives the feast, and it is the feast Yahusha (Jesus) sits down to when he takes the bread. The table in Matthew is the table Moses was given.
3033.phrase: spake unto Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt
3033.sentence: The Passover begins with Yahuah (LORD) speaking to Moses and Aaron in Egypt, the feast being kept at the supper.

3034.prose: Moses sprinkled the people with blood and said *blood of the covenant* over it. At the table Yahusha (Jesus) gives the bread as his body and speaks of his blood the same way, so the supper stands in the covenant meal Moses began and does not replace it.
3034.phrase: Behold the blood of the covenant, which Yahuah (LORD) hath made with you
3034.sentence: Moses names the blood of the covenant over the people, the words the supper takes up again.

3035.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) calls the bread his body at a table where a new covenant is being named. Jeremiah says who it is made with: *the house of Yashar'el (Israel)* and *the house of Yahudah (Judah)*, the two houses of one people. It is made with them, not put in their place.
3035.phrase: make a new covenant with the house of Yashar'el (Israel), and with the house of Yahudah (Judah)
3035.sentence: The new covenant is made with both houses of the one people, which is who sits at the supper.

3036.prose: Isaiah says Yahuah (LORD) makes his soul *an offering for sin*, and that he *shall see his seed*. Yahusha (Jesus) breaking the bread and calling it his body is that offering being given, and the seed it is given for are his own people.
3036.phrase: when thou shalt make his soul an offering for sin, he shall see his seed
3036.sentence: The soul made an offering for sin is the body given at the table, and the offered one has a seed.

3037.prose: John named him at the river before any of this: the Lamb. So when Yahusha (Jesus) breaks bread at the Passover and says *my body*, the lamb of the feast is the one at the table, and it was said of him first by the river.
3037.phrase: Behold the Lamb of Elohim (God), which taketh away the sin of the world
3037.sentence: John names the one at the table as the Lamb of Elohim (God) who takes away sin.

3038.prose: Long before the supper Yahusha (Jesus) had said the bread he would give was his flesh. At the Passover he takes the bread and says *this is my body*, and what he promised in John is what he hands round.
3038.phrase: the bread that I will give is my flesh, which I will give for the life of the world
3038.sentence: The bread he promised to give is his flesh, and at the table he gives it.

3039.prose: Paul puts the lamb and the bread together. Messiah (Christ) is the passover that is sacrificed, and the next lines tell them to keep the feast with unleavened bread. The supper in Matthew is the Passover kept, with the lamb named.
3039.phrase: For even Messiah (Christ) our passover is sacrificed for us
3039.sentence: Paul names Messiah (Christ) as the passover lamb, which is who the bread at the table speaks of.

3040.prose: In Revelation John sees a Lamb standing in the middle of the throne *as it had been slain*. The body broken over the bread at the Passover table is the body of that Lamb, and the one who gave it is the one John sees standing.
3040.phrase: stood a Lamb as it had been slain
3040.sentence: The Lamb that stands as though slain is the one whose body was given at the table.

3041.prose: The loud cry in Revelation is for the Lamb that was slain. The body given at the Passover table is the one they call worthy, and what began as bread in his hands ends with a great voice giving him honour and glory before the throne.
3041.phrase: Worthy is the Lamb that was slain to receive power
3041.sentence: Heaven cries out that the slain Lamb is worthy, the one whose body was given at the supper.

3042.prose: At the table Yahusha (Jesus) sets the cup down until a day he names, and here that day has come. The marriage of the Lamb is the feast he was waiting for, and his wife has made herself ready.
3042.phrase: for the marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife hath made herself ready
3042.sentence: The marriage of the Lamb is the feast the supper looks ahead to, with his wife ready.

3043.prose: The supper in Matthew looks ahead to a bigger table. Yahuah (LORD) lays a feast on the mountain for *all people*, and Yahusha (Jesus) says he will drink the cup new in his Father's kingdom. The Passover kept in the upper room points to that feast.
3043.phrase: make unto all people a feast of fat things, a feast of wines on the lees
3043.sentence: Isaiah's mountain feast is the table the supper looks forward to.

3045.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) is again speaking in parables, and the one that follows is a king making a wedding feast for his son. The bread in the upper room sits in the same line of talk: a table set, a feast made ready, and those bidden to come.
3045.phrase: spake unto them again by parables
3045.sentence: This opening of the wedding parable has Yahusha (Jesus) speaking of a feast prepared, as he does at the supper.

3046.prose: In Leviticus 16 Aaron may come into the holy place only with blood and an offering. Yahuah (LORD) speaks to Moses about how the blood is to come near, and at the Passover table Yahusha (Jesus) speaks of his body and his blood. The Torah's way with blood is not set aside here. The supper stands in it.
3046.phrase: spake unto Moses after the death of the two sons of Aaron
3046.sentence: Yahuah (LORD) tells Moses how blood and offering come near, the Torah the supper keeps standing.

3047.prose: Torah says what blood is for: the life is in it, and it makes atonement. When Yahusha (Jesus) calls the bread his body and goes on to speak of his blood, he speaks as Torah speaks. The blood is given *to make an atonement for your souls*, and the cup is no break from that.
3047.phrase: the life of the flesh is in the blood: and I have given it to you upon the altar
3047.sentence: The life is in the blood and it is given for atonement, which is what the cup speaks of.

7112.prose: Luke seats the twelve at the table, and Matthew shows what was done there. Yahusha (Jesus) takes bread, blesses it, breaks it and hands it to the disciples, saying it is his body. The twelve sat down to the Passover and were given the bread.
7112.phrase: took bread, and blessed it, and brake it, and gave it to the disciples
7112.sentence: Matthew shows the bread taken, blessed, broken and given to the disciples Luke has seated at the table.

5311.prose: Moses sprinkled the people and said *Behold the blood of the covenant*. At Mark's table Yahusha (Jesus) gives the bread as his body, and the cup that follows is spoken of the same way, so the supper stands in the covenant Moses cut and does not replace it.
5311.phrase: Behold the blood of the covenant, which Yahuah (LORD) hath made with you
5311.sentence: Moses names the blood of the covenant over the people, the words the supper takes up again.

5310.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) gives the bread as his body at a table where a new covenant is being named. Jeremiah says who it is made with: *the house of Yashar'el (Israel)* and *the house of Yahudah (Judah)*, the two houses of one people. It is made with them, not put in their place.
5310.phrase: make a new covenant with the house of Yashar'el (Israel), and with the house of Yahudah (Judah)
5310.sentence: The new covenant is made with both houses of the one people, which is who sits at the supper.

5312.prose: Paul passes on what Mark records. The night he was betrayed, Yahusha (Jesus) took bread, and Paul says he received this and gave it on. Two witnesses, one supper, the same night.
5312.phrase: the same night in which he was betrayed took bread
5312.sentence: Paul delivers the same supper of the night of the betrayal that Mark records.
